On Tue, February 26, 2008 16:51, Paul Lesniewski wrote:
> On Tue, Feb 26, 2008 at 7:35 AM, Fredrik Jervfors
>  wrote:
>
>>>> The debian control files can use a watch function to inform the
>>>> maintainer (me in this case) if there is a new version available. It
>>>> uses a kind of regexp to check a web directory, e.g. [snip]
>>
>>>>
>>>> Is it somehow possible to access the download location of SM
>>>> plugins without using the www.sm.org/plugins.php in general? This
>>>> could make my work much easier (I'm packaging additional SM
>>>> plugins).
>>
>> Nothing comes to mind, but I'm sure we can set something up. Do you
>> have any special considerations? If I know how the Debian script works,
>> I can
>> fix something that delivers the desired results (I hope). You can
>> contact me off-list if you don't want to clutter the mailing list with
>> the technical details.
>
> Please keep the conversation here or at least Cc: me since I'd like to
> be aware of any needed features, since I'd like to include any needed
> features in the feature list for the new plugins website we have been
> planning (don't hold your breath just yet though).

What is needed for this script to work is a web page where the URL to the
tarball can be found directly. The current setup needs you to first find
an URL with the right id= and rev=, and at that page find the link to the
tarball.

Two possible solutions:

* A page like this:
http://www.squirrelmail.org/plugin_view.php?id=256
could use direct links to the tarball instead of via a subpage.

* On pages like this:
http://www.squirrelmail.org/plugin_download.php?id=256&rev=1319
we could add the feature that leaving out "rev=????" always gives you a
link to the most recent tarball.

The first one seems better to me since the subpage seems a bit superfluous
in modern times. People can download tarballs nowadays, can they?


Thijs
